verdict: Spending is live but blind — no lead tracking means you cannot tell if $2,330 produced members.
diagnosis: Spend reached $2,330 this period with no lead, conversion, or pipeline data visible to judge whether the PCOS and Postpartum campaign is working.

signals.headline: Spent $2,330 across 28 days
signals.detail: One Facebook lead campaign targeting PCOS and postpartum ran this period. No leads or conversions reported back.

signals.headline: Daily spend averaged $13.63
signals.detail: That is below the $600 to $1,000 monthly floor most studios need to exit the Meta learning phase.

signals.headline: Latest day spend dropped to $3.85
signals.detail: Pacing fell sharply at period end. Either the budget throttled, the campaign paused, or delivery stalled.

signals.headline: Zero data from 4 of 5 sources
signals.detail: No Google profile, social, pipeline, or top performer feeds. The campaign is running without a feedback loop.

recommendations.title: Turn on lead tracking before adding budget
recommendations.detail: Confirm the Facebook lead form is firing and leads flow into a CRM or spreadsheet. Without lead counts, you cannot calculate cost per lead or judge the campaign.

recommendations.title: Investigate why daily spend dropped to $3.85
recommendations.detail: Check if the campaign is budget-capped, paused, or losing delivery. A $13 daily average is already thin for a studio lead campaign.

recommendations.title: Consider raising budget before January price spike
recommendations.detail: October leads are materially cheaper than January leads in fitness. Worth testing a modest budget lift now if lead quality is proven.
